seasonality_hint: Select a municipality on the map to see monthly seasonality.

dlnm.autocorr_warning: ⚠ This model (state-level) showed significant residual autocorrelation — treat the confidence interval as approximate, not a statistically definitive estimate. See docs/DATA_MODEL.md.

interpret.timeseries: Each point is the indicator's value on a given day. Hover over the line to see the exact value. Peaks and trends over time can indicate climate events (heatwaves/coldwaves) or seasonality.
interpret.comparison: Municipalities ranked from highest to lowest value (top 15) within the selected region/state. Useful for spotting outliers — municipalities with values well above their surroundings.
interpret.seasonality: Each box summarizes the indicator's values for that month, one per available year: the center line is the median, the box spans the middle 50%, and points beyond the whiskers are atypical years. Helps identify seasonal patterns (higher temperatures in Sep-Oct, rainfall during the wet season) and how much that pattern varies from year to year.
interpret.dlnm_overall: Cumulative relative risk (all lags combined) as a function of temperature, for the whole state containing the selected municipality — not a municipality-specific estimate. RR=1 (dashed line) is the reference (the state's historical median). The shaded band is the 95% confidence interval; the dots mark the 25/50/75/90/95/99th percentiles of observed temperature.
interpret.dlnm_lag: Relative risk isolated by day of lag (0 to 21 days after exposure), at the state's 75th percentile temperature. Shows how many days after a hot day the mortality risk shows up — useful to tell whether the effect is immediate or delayed.
interpret.dlnm_surface: Heatmap combining temperature (vertical axis) and lag (horizontal axis): red = elevated risk (log RR > 0), blue = reduced risk (log RR < 0) at that combination. Gives the full picture of where in the temperature x time grid the effect is strongest.
